audit.why: Level 6, Nashor's, and his late Abyssal Dive roam window are the right spikes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly sells a 'third-stack Q stun into Devour' chain. He cannot do both off the same stacks.
audit.why: Riot text: An Acquired Taste lets him use Devour at three stacks; Tongue Lash stuns a champion who already has 3 stacks and consumes them. So at three stacks he picks one payoff — stun or swallow — and the stun spends the resource the Devour needed.
audit.corrected: Every instance rewritten as a choice at three stacks, which is also the actual play rule: leave Q range at two stacks.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds timing in the prose despite two heal sources.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions: Tongue Lash heals him on champion hit and Thick Skin converts stored damage into healing out of combat.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Tongue Lash is 7/6.5/6/5.5/5s and Abyssal Dive 21s at rank 1 — the dive is the real punish window.
audit.corrected: Tongue Lash's 7s added to the do's.

edits.before: He still has only the stacked Q-into-Devour as a combo and you have no escape - it is a standoff where whoever respects the stun window wins it.
edits.after: At three stacks he must choose: stun with Tongue Lash or Devour you, since the stun consumes them - a standoff decided by who tracks the stack count.

edits.before: His only kill threat is stacking An Acquired Taste with autos/Q, then landing the third-stack Q stun to lock you for a Devour all-in - last-hit at max range, watch your stack count, and never sit in Q range with two stacks on you.
edits.after: His kill threat is three stacks of An Acquired Taste - at three he can stun with Tongue Lash or Devour you, never both, because the stun eats the stacks. Last-hit at max range and leave Q range the moment you carry two.

edits.before: Tahm Kench cannot kill you in a straight trade - his damage is grey-health drain, not burst - so the entire early game is just not eating the stun. His passive, An Acquired Taste, loads stacks on you with every auto and Q, and the third stack turns his next Tongue Lash into a stun that sets up a Devour all-in - that one window is his only way to delete a fragile pre-6 Kayle. Hold your ground at max last-hit range, watch your stack count, and step out of Q range the moment you are at two stacks rather than feeding the third-stack lockdown. If he never lands the loaded Q, his autos and Thick Skin just can't out-damage you in a poke war.
edits.after: Tahm Kench cannot kill you in a straight trade - his damage is drain, not burst - so the entire early game is just not eating the stun. His passive, An Acquired Taste, loads stacks on you with every auto and Q, and at three stacks he picks one payoff: a Tongue Lash stun, which consumes them, or a Devour. Either is his only way to delete a fragile pre-6 Kayle. Hold your ground at max last-hit range, watch your stack count, and step out of Q range at two rather than handing him the third. If he never loads three, his autos and Thick Skin can't out-damage you in a poke war.

edits.before: Level 6 is your flip: Divine Ascent turns your autos into ranged AoE magic waves and Divine Judgment hands you a few seconds of invulnerability, so a stacked Q-into-Devour no longer threatens a kill - you R the eat and walk out untouched. From here you kite. His Thick Skin grey health regenerates a chunk after trades, so don't try to burst him in one go; instead chip him from range repeatedly with Starfire Spellblade's missing-health magic on-hit, which shreds tanky HP faster than his grey health can refund it. Keep your distance and respect the Acquired Taste stacks - if he reloads the third-stack Q and gets on top of you, the stun still lets him Devour, so play around the stack count.
edits.after: Level 6 is your flip: Divine Ascent turns your autos into ranged AoE magic waves and Divine Judgment hands you a few seconds of invulnerability, so a Devour no longer threatens a kill - you R the eat and walk out untouched. From here you kite. Thick Skin converts stored damage into a shield and heals him out of combat, so don't try to burst him in one go; chip him from range repeatedly with Starfire Spellblade's missing-health on-hit, which shreds tanky HP faster than that refund. Keep your distance and count Acquired Taste stacks - at three he can stun you or swallow you outright, so never step up carrying two.

edits.before: You win the 1v1 outright by now - your Starfire missing-health waves under Divine Judgment invulnerability melt his stacked-HP drain-tank profile, and unlike a true scaler (Vlad, Kassadin, Vayne) Tahm has no way to reclaim this window. His real threat is map pressure, not lane: Abyssal Dive plus a flanking Devour lets him cross the map and pick a carry from fog. The moment he vanishes, ping it and assume he is surfacing somewhere - your job is to take the lane, snowball off winning the 1v1, and let your invulnerability ult deny the engage his Devour tries to set up for his team.
edits.after: You win the 1v1 outright by now - your Starfire missing-health waves under Divine Judgment melt his stacked-HP drain-tank profile, and Tahm has no way to reclaim this window. Carry Grievous Wounds: Tongue Lash heals him on every champion hit and Thick Skin refunds more out of combat. His real threat is map pressure, not lane: Abyssal Dive plus a flanking Devour lets him cross the map and pick a carry from fog. The moment he vanishes, ping it and assume he is surfacing somewhere - take the lane, and let your ult deny the engage his Devour sets up for his team.

notes: The stun-into-Devour chain the page sold does not exist: three stacks buy either the Tongue Lash stun (which consumes them) or the Devour, not both. Devour itself has no cooldown in Riot's data — it is gated purely by the 100 mana and the stacks. The packet's five suspectNames here are all false positives; Starfire Spellblade, An Acquired Taste, Radiant Blast and Divine Ascent are all correct as written.
